solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heron is flying close to coast

indicators.note: letters that fly scatter and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A heron takes off and skims along near the shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: The heron is a real shore bird, so the surface looks like a nature note; its name is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fishing boats working inshore stay in the waters near the land rather than out at sea.

clue.text: After reorganization, the CID had a restless urge

indicators.note: reorganizing the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A shake-up of the detective squad leaves its officers restless.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurative sense of the skin sensation: someone itching to leave cannot keep still for wanting to go.

clue.text: Insect’s obsession with diluted drink?

blocks.note: a British fruit cordial, mixed with water before drinking
a craze, as in 'the travel bug'

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: is this insect simply obsessed with fruit cordial?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the insect's name backwards into a fondness: a 'bug for squash'. The question mark owns up to the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by name: the squash bug is a real sap-sucking pest of pumpkins and marrows, named after the vegetable, not the drink.

clue.text: Play with books and magazine

blocks.note: the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone passes the time reading books and a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about amusing yourself with reading matter; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shakespeare's tragedy of the jealous Moor is one play among many.

clue.text: Male comedians wearing alien paraphernalia?

indicators.note: the comedians put the alien on around them, so ET goes outside

blocks.note: men who make quips, an invented word

explanation.surface: A troupe of comics dressed in alien costumes and props.
explanation.walkthrough: The comedians are a coinage, which is why the clue needs its question mark; a real word for them would never fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words cover the kit and gear needed for an activity, paraphernalia with a hint of clutter.

clue.text: Charge leaders of illegal group infiltrating island

indicators.note: the leaders of a line of words are their front letters
to infiltrate is to get inside, so these letters go into the island

blocks.note: Arran, an island in the Firth of Clyde off western Scotland

explanation.surface: The heads of an outlaw gang slip onto an island and are charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' could be a cavalry rush or a fee; the gang story points it at a court, which is the right sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term: to arraign is to bring someone before a court and read out the charge against them.

clue.text: Cook near a stadium

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, and cooked letters are tampered with

explanation.surface: An instruction to do your cooking close to a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as an order to make a meal; it is the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the sand-strewn floor of a Roman amphitheatre, now any enclosed venue for sport or concerts.

clue.text: Dish with a bit of ginger is Ottoman

indicators.note: the answer is a bit of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'ginger' into 'Ottoman'

explanation.surface: A recipe claims that a dish with a pinch of ginger is Turkish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'a bit of ginger' a pinch of spice; it means a stretch of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this creamy Italian rice cooked slowly in stock is one kind of dish.

clue.text: Private tavern supported by the Queen

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that supports another sits below it

explanation.surface: A soldier's pub enjoys royal patronage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one's inner life or inner thoughts are the private ones kept from others.

clue.text: Not a chance advert bores son currently

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the advert goes inside

explanation.surface: A grumble that there's no hope of an advert not boring your son these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' reads as 'tires out', which fits a dull advert; it means drills into. The insertion splits the phrase after its W.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean at the present time, as opposed to in the past.

clue.text: It’s on course to beat audience

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: the building found on a golf course

blocks.note: to hit with a heavy stick
a theatre audience, as in 'a full house'

explanation.surface: Someone is on track to outdo the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On course' reads as 'on track'; it is literal, a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the building where golfers change and drink stands on the course itself.

clue.text: Is returning with fresh strength

indicators.note: going back turns the letters round

explanation.surface: Someone comes back feeling reinvigorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with the bare word 'Is', which is fodder rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the tendon that ties muscle to bone stands for muscular power, as in 'the sinews of war'.

clue.text: Pop producer drops initial support for artist?

indicators.note: the word lets go of its initial, its first letter

explanation.surface: A pop record producer loses his first backing for a new act.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme goes 'Pop goes the weasel', so the weasel produces the pop. 'Pop producer' and 'artist' both pretend to be music business.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the wooden stand holds up a painter's canvas while they work, and the question mark admits 'artist' is not a singer.

clue.text: Drunk did some decorating

blocks.note: a slang adjective for very drunk
a past-tense verb: smoothed a wall with its finishing coat

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk while redecorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' can be a past tense verb, but it is the adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: slang for heavily intoxicated, and the past tense of coating walls, a decorating job.

clue.text: The boy with no logic developed “vital” industry

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters; 'with' joins the pieces

explanation.surface: An illogical lad grew up to build an essential industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital' is in quotes because it is used in its root sense, to do with life, which is what bio- means.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on the Latin root: vital means relating to life, and this is the industry built on living cells.

clue.text: Friend’s after short string instrument and wind instrument

indicators.note: the friend comes after the other piece
short means missing its last letter

blocks.note: one of the six in the TV sitcom Friends; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A band line-up: one person on something stringed, another on a wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F is the tell: the Friend is Monica Geller from the sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the mouth organ sounds when you blow or draw breath through its reeds.

clue.text: Islander’s monkey ran off

indicators.note: letters that go off are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A man on an island watches his pet monkey escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Orkney is an island group off the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a man from the Orkney archipelago is one kind of islander.

clue.text: Farm labourer catches start of hockey game

indicators.note: the labourer holds the letter inside
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A farmhand grabs the ball at the opening of a hockey match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the hockey match; it means birds hunted for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: game is wild animals shot for sport and the table, and the pheasant is the commonest game bird.

clue.text: Apex of road unfinished? Call boat!

indicators.note: the word is left without its last letter

blocks.note: to call something by a name is to term it

explanation.surface: A stranded traveller at the top of an unfinished road phones for a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The break between the wordplay pieces falls in the middle of WATER, so the answer's shape does not help.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the line left by the highest tide becomes the peak of any achievement.

clue.text: Get rid of stated reason to look peevish?

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: asking the reason for a sulky face

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the excuse for a sulky face to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason to look peevish?' is a playful way of asking the reason for a pout, and the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to destroy completely, as a wiped-out debt or army is gone for good.

clue.text: Robot’s revolutionary make-up famous designer reverse-engineered

indicators.note: revolving turns the letters round
reversed, then built into the answer

blocks.note: DIOR, the fashion house, turned round

explanation.surface: A robot's radical design was copied by taking apart a famous designer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' reads as cosmetics beside a fashion designer; it is genetic make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: from the Greek for 'manlike', it names a robot built to look human.

clue.text: Union member pockets building’s last spanner

indicators.note: to pocket is to take inside
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trade unionist on a building site steals the last wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union member' suggests a trade union and 'spanner' a tool; the union is marriage, and a spanner is something that spans.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: anything that spans a gap is a spanner, and a bridge spans a river or road.

clue.text: Article with piece of advice regarding Italian food

explanation.surface: A magazine piece offers advice about Italian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a magazine feature; it is the grammar word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Italian word means 'before the meal', the cold starter of meats and olives.

clue.text: Mark 2?

blocks.note: reads as a model name, but is the pen name of an American author
reads as a version number, but is the number in an old word

explanation.surface: It looks like the label on a second version of a product.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark 2 usually means a second model; read it as the author of Tom Sawyer, whose surname is the archaic word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue works twice: Samuel Clemens wrote as Mark Twain, and 'twain' is old English for the number two.

clue.text: Decline small piece of sugar, say

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
a cube of sugar; 'say' marks sugar as one example

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a sugar lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refusing the sugar; it is the fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prices or form that slump drop suddenly and stay low.

clue.text: Romeo, consumed by love, is gloomy

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed inside the other word

explanation.surface: Romeo, eaten up by love, is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo fits the love story perfectly, but he is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary variant: poets clip dreary to drear, keeping its sense of dull and cheerless.

clue.text: Last couple leaving fashionable site in Texas

indicators.note: a couple is two, so the last two letters are the ones walking out

blocks.note: A LA MODE without its last two letters

explanation.surface: The final pair walk out of a trendy venue in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last couple' looks like two people; it means the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by place: the old San Antonio mission, besieged in 1836, is Texas's most famous historic site.

clue.text: Ignorant to expel knight wearing official regalia?

indicators.note: the letter is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: UNINFORMED without an N, knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: An ignorant order to throw out a knight in full ceremonial dress.
explanation.walkthrough: N is knight in chess notation; either N of the longer word can go.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose fit, flagged by the question mark: regalia are ceremonial trappings, and a uniform is official dress.

clue.text: Track user with first-class bit of gear?

blocks.note: an armoured vehicle running on caterpillar tracks

explanation.surface: Spying on a user with the best piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' reads as follow or a running track; it is the tread of an armoured vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear as slang for clothes: in Britain a tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover, one item of clothing.

clue.text: Colonist enters mountain range mostly at a gentle pace

indicators.note: the colonist goes into the range
most of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A settler walks slowly into the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonist' suggests a settler; it is an insect that lives in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction: Italian for 'walking', it marks a moderate, unhurried tempo.
